Sure, there's institutional adoption but they get most of upside without buying our coins. 

Thus betting on that adoption via tokens is meh: upside seems to be in equity or private markets. 

Crypto was supposed to solve this!

Cosmos ATOM provided core ledger technology for shitloads of companies and they are basically dead.

BTC would pump if there was money printing in sight but that won't happen until AI bubble collapses:

and that would first rekt crypto as well. 

(I would've thought differently but AI crashing and rebounded while crypto crashed without rebound is making us all bearish).

Meanwhile trenches are rekt beyond believe. Pump, FOMO & grifters are running out of dumb money and backlash on X is getting louder.

Mid to long term it's clear that crypto is here to stay.

But we'll be tested by 1) democrats getting their vandetta on crypto and 2) interest rates increasing that can't be good for risk assets.

The most bullish point about this post is that it sounds so bearish, and usually when one wants to sell is the best time to buy?

Figma jumped 250% on IPO day, but by November 9th, buyers were down 83%

A useful reality check ahead of Anthropic’s IPO

I unpack the benchmark, what it could mean for Anthropic + how crypto feeds into this in issue #201 of my newsletter

Dont invest with money you need short term

Perspective provides clarity 

IF as people argue there is no interest in BTC right now due to AI etc and its STILL above 70k - how cool is that?

5 yrs ago when it was 70k it was off the back of alot of leverage and speculation

Asymmetry is often found when interest in an asset is low despite growth

The argument that BTC is boring and therefore they should buy AI which is what everyone is interested in goes against any fundamental investing principle - basically saying "buy consensus, buy the speculation"

The argument to buy any asset should be one based on asymmetry whether consensus or not - not based on interest

Same is true of gold 5 years ago - it had no interest despite growing central bank interest and then instead people lined up to buy when it was 5000 an ounce

No interest doesnt mean it will do well either but you have to be able to discern what matters and what doesnt 

Public sentiment and anecdotes should not form the basis for investing - some people do well with this trading short term but you cant mix these together when looking at decade time horizons
